comparison_limits: These are initial visible comparisons, not proposed quality criteria, construction choices, self-ratings, or approval.
No future camera, world size, footprint, envelope, ground contact, material lock, part-count lock or motion contract was inferred from target pixels or generic tile rules.

Original geometry, old materials, object count and faceting are observations rather than automatic aesthetic locks; useful design improvements remain within user-authorized modeling freedom once ROOT freezes the real contract.
fixed_target: The target preserves the recognizable blue/purple scattered reef-fragment identity and nine main fragment arrangement, while the main stones read as fuller irregular crystal chunks.

Cream to pale yellow highlights gather on top faces, upper edges and selected corners; the blue stones gain cyan upper planes and teal lower planes, while purple stones gain lavender upper planes and deeper violet lower planes.

Many facet joins are accented with narrow light lines. Small separate matching companion chips appear beside the main fragments. The target has richer surface lighting and thicker-looking volumes than the original.
Some target edges read crisp or glossy; those visible accents are an aesthetic reference, not evidence of camera, contact, geometry-envelope or animation requirements.
global_style: The actual global reference is a bright green angular-leaf plant in a warm orange-gold square pot. Broad highlights, shaded leaf overlaps, softened pot rims and warm surface light make the volume readable.
The leaf planes retain clear angular structure while their tonal changes are broad and the pot has thick, softly rounded edges. This combines simplified forms with depth and soft light.

Its shape language is simpler and its face highlights broader than the target crystal seam accents. The reference informs the requested warm, softly lit cartoon treatment without changing the fragment identity or blue/purple palette.
original: Nine detached angular main fragments are visible: five purple and four blue, spread around an open center with no connecting surface.
The silhouettes vary in elongation and rotation. Each main fragment has a small set of conspicuous triangular light/dark faces and sharp corners.
The palette is strongly blue/violet with darker lower or side faces and relatively restrained highlights. No companion chips or painted seam network are visible in the original.
